neighbours.label: the modifier of a material compound, where the head is predictable (tooth[-colored], oat/wheat/corn [flour/dough])
fire: The clinic offers tooth-colored fillings instead of metal ones.
Small chips can be repaired with a tooth-colored composite.
Ask your dentist whether a tooth-colored veneer would suit you.
For a nuttier loaf, swap half the white flour for oat flour.
Mix the corn flour with cold water before adding it to the soup.
The tortillas are pressed by hand from fresh corn dough.
You can replace some of the wheat flour with almond flour.
Sift the wheat flour and the baking powder into a large bowl.
quiet: The clinic offers white ceramic fillings instead of metal ones.
Small chips can be repaired by the dentist in one visit.
Ask your dentist whether a porcelain veneer would suit you.
For a nuttier loaf, add a handful of chopped walnuts.
Mix the cream with cold water before adding it to the soup.
The tortillas are pressed by hand and cooked on a hot stone.
Farmers in the valley grow wheat, oats and a little corn.
Brush your teeth twice a day and replace the brush often.

notes: Probe: 'tooth-colored resin' 0.77 (peak '-colored'), 'a tooth-colored crown' 0.45 (peak ' tooth'), 'with oat flour' 0.40 (peak ' oat'), 'corn dough' 0.35, 'wheat flour' 0.26, 'a second coat' 0.23; 'harvested the wheat' 0.003, 'pulled the tooth' 0.07, recipes without a grain modifier 0.05-0.08. Two near misses keep the bare grain and tooth words as plain nouns (crops, teeth) to test the word without the compound.
